title: For a horses-for-temporary-entry notification the hub's Exit details row reads "Cannot start yet" and never changes, and the port of exit and exit date are asked nowhere on the way through — the only route to them is re-opening the reason page, which nothing signposts; DR1 asks both on the reason page itself.

finding.frontend: The hub shows an "Exit details" row under "1. About the consignment" with the hint "Where the consignment travels on to and when it leaves Great Britain", no link, and the status "Cannot start yet" — while every other row on the same page, including Additional commodity details and Uploaded documents, is a working link. That combination pins the state down. A row is offered only if the first page behind it passes, and the Exit details row's first page is Destination country (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39, src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25). Pages later in the flow than Destination country are open, so the block is not a missing earlier answer; it is that the destination-country question is out of scope. The row is nonetheless shown rather than hidden, which only happens when at least one of its three questions is in scope (controller.js:93). The single reason for import that puts the port of exit and the exit date in scope while leaving the destination country out is "For horses authorised for temporary entry" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:61-116). Because the row's status is overwritten with "Cannot start yet" regardless of progress (controller.js:95), it would still read that way after the questions were answered, and because the opening run steps from the reason page past the exit questions to animal identification (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39) a first-time user is never asked them on the way through. The one route left is to re-open "Main reason for importing" from the hub and press "Save and continue", which walks on to the port of exit and then the exit date. Nothing on the hub says so, and until those two answers exist the Check and submit row is blocked too, so a user who trusts the task list has no way of knowing what is holding the notification up.
finding.prototype: DR1 has no exit-details task. The port of exit and the exit date are conditional reveals on the radios of the reason-for-import page (app/views/reason-for-import.html:47-62, whose four reveal blocks are supplied at app/routes.js:8778-8784), so choosing temporary admission of horses shows both questions immediately, on the page where the choice was made, and the hub's "Main reason for import" row covers them.
finding.difference: Make the row's availability follow the questions that are actually in scope rather than the first page listed against it — the row should open on Port of exit when Destination country does not apply — and stop overwriting a blocked row's status, so a completed exit-details row reads Completed. The wider structural difference, that DR1 asks all four reason-dependent questions inline on one page while the frontend splits them across four, is a separate change owned by the origin-and-reason slice; this finding is only about the hub row being shut and the questions behind it being unsignposted.
finding.falsifiedBy: A frontend hub capture for a notification whose reason for import is horses authorised for temporary entry in which the Exit details row is a link, or in which it reads Completed after the port of exit and exit date have been given.
finding.verification: Opened the fe-hub-exit-details-blocked and dr1-notification-hub DOMs and both screenshots, the DR1 dr1-reason-for-import-temporary-admission-horses-revealed DOM, and read task-rows.js:27-59, flow/navigation.js:20-37, flow/gates.js:23-32, flow/prerequisites.js, hub/controller.js:93-123, obligations/sections/import-reason.js:34-116, linear/flow/flow.js:44-58, linear/flow/run.js:22-53, shared/kit.js:77-101, shared/save-actions.njk and features/import-reason/{controller.js:55-82,template.njk}. This is the finding carrying the declared contamination, so I re-derived every leg from the evidence and the source without reference to any earlier run. INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED. (1) The row is dead in the capture: `<li class="govuk-task-list__item">` with a bare <div> title and `govuk-task-list__status--cannot-start-yet` reading "Cannot start yet", while Main reason for importing above it reads Completed and every other row is a link. (2) The mechanism: `rowGatePasses = pageGatePasses(row.pages[0], scope)` and the exitDetails row's pages[0] is destinationCountryPage, so the row's availability is decided by a question the user does not have. (3) The reason: import-reason.js gates destinationCountry to {transit, transhipmentOrOnwardTravel}, portOfExit to {transit, temporaryAdmissionHorses} and exitDate to temporaryAdmissionHorses alone, so temporaryAdmissionHorses is the only value that puts two of the three in scope and leaves the first out — the author's claim, confirmed from the obligation source. (4) The row shows rather than hides because `statusOf` returns NA only when no part is in scope (bridge/status/index.js:87-91) and two of the three are. (5) `blockedRowItem` discards the computed status, so the row would still read "Cannot start yet" once answered. RE-RAN THE REACHABILITY CLAIM, which is the one worth doubting. The opening run really does skip the exit questions: RUN_STEPS is origin, commodities, consignment-details, import-reason, import-purpose, animal-identification, additional-details, and import-purpose's own gate fails for this reason, so the user goes reason -> identification and is never shown either question. After the hub GET calls `completeOpeningRun`, `nextTarget` falls through `runTarget` (null, run over) to `nextInSection`, whose section for import-reason is `consignment` = [importReason, importPurpose, destinationCountry, portOfExit, exitDate, additionalDetails]; import-purpose and destination-country both fail `inScopeReachable`, so the next gate-passing page is Port of exit. The primary "Save and continue" button carries no `exit` name (save-actions.njk:5), so `hubExitTarget` does not divert it — only the secondary "Save and return" does. The author's claimed route therefore holds, and I confirmed it from the flow code rather than from the row. RUBRIC 2 FIRED on the strength of the wording: the previous title said the user "is never offered the port of exit or exit date from the hub" and the frontend slot ended "from the hub alone the notification cannot be finished", which contradicts the route the same sentence names — the reason row is on the hub and pressing Save and continue on it reaches both questions, so the notification can be finished from the hub, just not by anything the task list tells the user. Narrowed the title and that clause; the mechanism, the reason-for-import identification and the DR1 side are unchanged. On the DR1 side I confirmed the reveals in the captured DOM rather than from the view alone: the temporary-admission capture carries `name="temporaryAdmissionExitDate"` labelled "Exit date" and `name="temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit"` labelled "Port of exit" inside the radio's conditional block, and the DR1 hub has no exit row of any kind.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: that a horses-for-temporary-entry user "is never offered the port of exit or exit date from the hub", and that "from the hub alone the notification cannot be finished". TRUE: the Exit details row never opens and never changes status, and neither question is asked on the way through — but the reason row on the same hub does lead to both questions on Save and continue, so the journey is completable from the hub; what is missing is any signpost, not the route. CHECKED by following nextTarget -> runTarget -> nextInSection through shared/kit.js:92-101 and flow/navigation.js:27-37 against the `consignment` section in linear/flow/flow.js:48-58, with the gate outcomes taken from import-reason.js. The claim is narrowed, not struck.

relatedTo.why: the same row gate, applied to a case where it never releases
